source: Sakana AI Fugu — Multi-Agent Orchestration as a Foundation Model
summary: Sakana released Fugu (June 2026), a family of orchestrator models trained with RL (TRINITY + Conductor) that coordinate a pool of LLMs behind a single OpenAI-compatible API. The coordinator assigns Thinker/Worker/Verifier roles dynamically and can call itself recursively.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocess agents with a deterministic state machine. The learned/RL orchestration approach requires ML training infrastructure far outside AgentForge's scope. Dynamic role assignment via trained model is architecturally incompatible with the explicit state machine design.

summary: MAF 1.0 (April 2026) merges AutoGen and Semantic Kernel. Ships sequential/concurrent/handoff orchestration patterns, checkpointing, pause/resume, YAML declarative config, middleware hooks, fan-in/fan-out, visual debugger, MCP support. AutoGen and Semantic Kernel enter maintenance mode.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — The middleware hooks pattern (intercept/transform agent behavior without modifying prompts) is conceptually interesting for AgentForge's policyEngine.ts. However, AgentForge already has explicit policy gates and the state machine achieves similar control. No clear gap to fill that isn't already tracked.

source: REMem — Reasoning with Episodic Memory in Language Agent (arXiv:2602.13530)
summary: REMem (Feb 2026) builds a two-phase framework for constructing and reasoning with episodic memory. Reports +3.4% and +13.4% absolute improvements over Mem0 and HippoRAG 2 on episodic recollection tasks.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — Maps to the cross-run episodic memory gap already tracked by HID-188. The two-phase construct/reason pattern could inform the HID-188 implementation.

source: Amory — Building Coherent Narrative-Driven Agent Memory (arXiv:2601.06282)
summary: Amory (Jan 2026) organizes conversational fragments into episodic narratives, consolidates memories with momentum, and semanticizes peripheral facts. Reports up to +27.8% over Mem0 combining episodic and semantic memory types.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — Also maps to HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory). The narrative consolidation approach could reduce memory fragmentation across AgentForge runs.

summary: Comprehensive survey of agent memory along three dimensions: memory substrate (internal/external), cognitive mechanism (episodic/semantic/sensory/working/procedural), and memory subject (agent-centric/user-centric). January–February 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Good framework for evaluating HID-188 design choices. No new actionable gap beyond what HID-188 already tracks.

source: Self-Harness — Agent Harness Self-Improvement Without External Engineer (arXiv:2606.09498)
summary: Self-Harness (June 2026) allows agents to improve their own harness (prompts, memory schemas, tool configurations) without a human engineer or stronger external agent. Tested on Terminal-Bench-2.0.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge's distillationAgent.ts already extracts skills from run outcomes. This extends to revising prompts and harness structure iteratively. Interesting direction but requires a foundation from HID-188 (episodic memory) and would be premature before that ships. Backlog also at cap.

source: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement / RHI (arXiv:2607.15524, Sakana AI + UC Berkeley)
summary: RHI (July 2026) treats the harness as a prompt-level specification and refines it using pairwise feedback on run outcomes. Can be applied to any agent harness without changing model weights.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Maps to AgentForge's distillation pipeline. Could extend distillationAgent.ts to include harness-level revisions (not just skills). Requires HID-188 as prerequisite. Backlog at cap.

source: RRSI — Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses (arXiv:2609.24972)
summary: RRSI (September 2026) adds regularization to harness evolution by constraining which candidate edits get proposed and selected, reporting better generalization to unseen benchmarks compared to unconstrained harness evolution.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — The regularization constraint is directly relevant to AgentForge's distillation: without constraints, skill distillation could overfit to recent runs and corrupt good patterns. This is a refinement of the harness self-improvement theme. Backlog at cap; worth revisiting after HID-188 ships.

summary: Describes harness self-evolution as revising prompts, memory, workflows and executable components while model weights stay fixed. October 2026 paper (unverified against arXiv directly).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Extends the harness self-improvement theme. If verified, this paper explicitly covers prompt + workflow revision without model changes, aligning with AgentForge's constraint of not retraining. Backlog at cap; revisit when backlog drains.

summary: LangGraph shipped 1.0 in Oct 2025, with continued 1.x updates through mid-2026. CrewAI reached v1.14-1.15 by April-May 2026. AutoGen entered maintenance mode; Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) 1.0 is the successor. No breaking new patterns beyond stateful workflows and checkpointing.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocess agents, not Python SDK frameworks. The checkpointing/pause-resume patterns from MAF are conceptually related to HID-186 (partial retry) but AgentForge's approach is state-machine-driven, not framework-library-driven.

source: Karpathy observations on code agents and agent-driven coding workflows (early 2026)
summary: Karpathy transitioned to fully agent-driven coding workflows (Claude Code) by Jan-Feb 2026. His MicroGPT (Feb 2026) is a 243-line GPT in pure Python. His commentary focuses on prompt-engineering agents and expressing intent rather than writing code — no specific new architectural innovations for orchestrators.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Reflects the broader shift AgentForge is already built for. No specific orchestration pattern or architectural gap identified beyond existing backlog items.
